business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Vessel Shipment of VHP Raw Cane Centrifugal Sugar

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Bilateral Investment Treaty, signed 30 May 1984 and in force subject to its terms
France-China Double Taxation Convention on income and capital, signed 30 September 1984, as amended
France-United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Convention, signed 19 July 1989, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT obligations arise under Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and related provisions of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), including customer identification, beneficial-owner identification, risk assessment, enhanced due diligence, suspicious-transaction reporting and record retention. The beneficial-owner definition is principally set out in Article R.561-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Beneficial-owner filing obligations for legal entities are governed principally by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 of that Code and related provisions of the Commercial Code. The historical beneficial-owner register framework was introduced by Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 and is now administered through the French National Business Register (Registre national des entreprises) maintained by the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding, payment-account opening and material transactions, screen the company, managers, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties, banks, vessels and major suppliers against United Nations sanctions, European Union sanctions, French national sanctions, applicable United States OFAC lists and relevant United Kingdom sanctions lists. Perform PEP, family-member and close-associate screening using reliable, documented sources. Apply enhanced due diligence for PEPs, opaque ownership, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual commodity routes, third-party payments, sanctions-sensitive vessels and trade-finance structures. Screening must be refreshed on a risk basis and upon ownership, management, vessel, counterparty or sanctions-list changes. A French reporting entity must file suspicious-transaction reports with TRACFIN where legally required; OFAC rules apply directly only where there is a United States nexus or another applicable legal basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), accessed through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the legal entity is recorded in the Registre national des entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the articles of association and filing in a form accepted under French law. French spelling and Latin characters are ordinarily accepted. A name may contain foreign-language terms, but it must not mislead the public, infringe prior rights, create confusion with an existing undertaking, or improperly imply a regulated status. The legal form designation such as Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL must be included as required in corporate documents and business-facing use. A French translation is required for supporting documents not drafted in French unless the receiving authority accepts another language.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a regulated financial, insurance, legal, accounting, educational or public function
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a separate statutory company-name reservation procedure with a universal reservation period. Conduct prior-rights, trademark, trade-name, domain-name and corporate-registry searches before filing. If the INPI one-stop shop or registry rejects or suspends the filing, obtain the formal deficiency or rejection notice, correct the name or supporting documents within the prescribed deadline, and resubmit through the portal. If the decision is maintained, request administrative review from the competent registry authority and, where appropriate, bring an action before the competent administrative or commercial court within the applicable procedural time limit. A trademark or unfair-competition dispute may require separate proceedings before the competent judicial court or the National Institute of Industrial Property.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SARL must have a declared registered office in France. Commercial domiciliation through an authorized domiciliation provider is generally permissible if the provider holds the required authorization and the domiciliation contract and supporting documents satisfy filing requirements. A virtual office does not replace operational substance. For wholesale physical sugar trading, the company should maintain documented management activity, accounting records, contracts, trade-finance files, customs and VAT evidence, supplier and customer due diligence, logistics records and decision-making capacity in France consistent with its declared business model. Banks, tax authorities, customs authorities and AML-regulated counterparties may reject a purely nominal address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection: approximately 1% to 5% for a newly formed, low-risk wholesale company with complete filings and no adverse indicators; approximately 5% to 15% where there are VAT-refund claims, customs anomalies, inconsistent substance, high-risk counterparties, unexplained payment flows or AML alerts. These are risk-management estimates, not statutory probabilities or official government statistics.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.123-1 et seq.; SARL formation, management, and capital rules are principally set out in Articles L.223-1, L.223-2, L.223-7, L.223-18, and L.223-30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Commercial and Companies Registry (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS), maintained by the clerk of the territorially competent Commercial Court (greffe du tribunal de commerce); company-creation formalities are submitted through the INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-creation formalité submitted through the Guichet unique, including executed articles of association (statuts) and the required declarations and supporting documents; successful filing results in RCS registration and issuance of a SIREN number and Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a SARL. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid on incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of RCS registration. Cash contributions are deposited before filing with an eligible depositary, such as a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and released upon proof of registration. Contributions in kind are generally fully contributed at formation; an auditor for contributions may be required, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: A SARL has no board of directors. The following initial decisions should be adopted by the founding shareholder(s) and recorded in the incorporation file: “The shareholder(s) resolve to incorporate [Company Name] as a société à responsabilité limitée under the attached articles of association; approve the subscription and allocation of the shares set out therein and acknowledge payment of the required portion of cash contributions; adopt [address] as the registered office; and appoint [name, address] as gérant, who accepts the appointment and is authorized to complete the registration formalities, open corporate accounts, and take actions necessary to commence business. The company shall assume, after registration, the commitments entered into on its behalf in accordance with applicable law.”

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm founders, name, activity, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises; INPI Name and Company Search databases; local Commercial and Companies Registry for territorial jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the company name, registered office, purpose, share allocations, manager, and business activity. Use a sufficiently precise corporate purpose covering wholesale trading and shipment of raw cane sugar. Obtain evidence of a lawful registered-office address and check name availability. No separate industrial license is required solely for wholesale sugar trading.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and corporate purpose
Registered-office evidence, such as a lease, title, or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct name conflicts, incomplete activity descriptions, or deficient address evidence before filing; amend the proposed name or provide replacement supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute articles of association and appoint the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholder(s); no government approval or notarization is ordinarily required for standard SARL articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the French-language articles of association, specifying capital, shares, contributions, management, registered office, and corporate purpose. Appoint the gérant in the articles or by a separate written decision. Obtain required declarations from the manager. Use a sworn French translation for foreign-language supporting records; apply apostille or legalization where required by the document’s country of origin and applicable treaty rules.
required_dossiers: Written manager appointment, if not included in the articles
Manager’s identification document and non-conviction/eligibility declaration
Foreign-document translations, apostilles, or legalizations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies between the articles, appointment decision, identity records, and online filing; execute a dated amendment or replacement document and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Eligible bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit at least 20% of subscribed cash contributions before filing and obtain the depositary’s certificate. The remaining cash contribution must be paid within five years after RCS registration. Document any contributions in kind in the articles and obtain a commissaire aux apports report unless a statutory exemption is validly available and elected.
required_dossiers: Executed draft or final articles of association
Founder identity and beneficial-ownership information requested by the depositary
Capital deposit instruction and proof of transfer
Valuation report or documented statutory exemption for contributions in kind, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank onboarding or AML queries with source-of-funds and ownership evidence; correct the deposit amount or contributor details and obtain a replacement certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-notice publication service for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed incorporation notice in an authorized journal or online legal-notice service in the department of the registered office. Ensure the notice matches the articles on company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, and manager. Obtain the publication attestation for the filing.
required_dossiers: Company particulars consistent with the executed articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction notice or republication if any mandatory particulars are omitted or inconsistent; upload the corrected attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises, routed to the competent RCS clerk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation formalité, upload the signed articles and supporting records, disclose beneficial owners through the required declaration, and pay applicable registry and beneficial-owner filing charges. The stated USD fee is an indicative conversion of French euro charges; actual charges and exchange rates may vary. Monitor the portal for requests for correction and retain the submission receipt.
required_dossiers: Manager appointment, identity, and eligibility declarations
Electronic filing receipt and payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the Guichet unique within the stated cure period, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional charge. If rejected, correct the identified defect and submit a new or amended formalité; use the available registry appeal procedure where legally appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique; Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des Finances publiques); relevant bank and social-security bodies as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Kbis extract and verify the SIREN, SIRET, and registered activity details. Provide the Kbis to the capital depositary to release funds. Confirm corporate tax and VAT registration details, activate accounting records, and update the RCS through the Guichet unique when registered particulars change. Assess separate customs, food-safety, or premises obligations based on the actual trading and storage model.
required_dossiers: Premises, import, customs, and product-compliance records where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of registry or tax-account errors through the relevant portal or authority; defer regulated premises operations until required local or sector-specific approvals are obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board or manufacturing authorization is ordinarily required for wholesale trading and vessel shipment of raw cane sugar. For a facility potentially subject to classified-installation controls, the competent authority is the Departmental Prefect, with applications handled by the relevant regional environmental inspectorate (DREAL, or the competent regional authority).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating or manufacturing permit is required solely for wholesale sugar trading. A separate premises-specific declaration, registration, or authorization may apply if storage or other site activities fall within the French classified installations regime (Installations classées pour la protection de l’environnement, ICPE).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; relevant regional environmental inspectorate (DREAL or competent regional authority); Departmental Prefect for ICPE decisions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not ordinarily applicable to wholesale sugar trading without a regulated facility. Any warehouse or handling site must be screened against applicable ICPE nomenclature and environmental assessment thresholds; the required procedure may be no filing, declaration, registration, or authorization with an environmental assessment, depending on the site and activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No activity-specific wastewater or VOC threshold is triggered solely by commodity trading. Any facility must comply with applicable ICPE permit conditions, water-discharge rules, air-emission limits, waste traceability and disposal requirements, and municipal sewer approvals. Avoid dust releases during handling and maintain appropriate containment and housekeeping; site-specific limits must be confirmed with the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general civil-defense clearance is required solely for wholesale trading. A warehouse must satisfy applicable building, fire-safety, and workplace rules; obtain planning and building approvals where required; maintain fire equipment and emergency procedures; and arrange workplace risk assessment and prevention measures. Public-access premises may require ERP fire-safety and accessibility compliance. Structural inspections and fire-authority review depend on the building classification, works, and use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — e-filing and VAT portal: impots.gouv.fr; business formalities single window (Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs, EORI and export-licence administration: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) at douane.gouv.fr; commercial register: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident shareholders establish the SARL through the electronic single window of the INPI. INSEE then issues the 9-digit SIREN, the 14-digit SIRET establishment number and the NAF/APE activity code. Following confirmation of the statutory registration, the DGFiP allocates the French intra-EU VAT identification number (format FR + two-digit control key + nine-digit SIREN) on the basis of the VAT registration application and the company's tax option; the VAT number must be stated on all invoices and on the EU recapitulative statement (ESA/DES). The company must simultaneously obtain an EORI number from the DGDDI for customs declarations and, if it trades within the EU, register for the Intrastat/DEB reporting framework. The Kbis extract issued by the RCS serves as the official proof of existence and of the legal representative's powers. Standard processing time is 2 to 6 weeks after the registration file is complete; the VAT number is usually delivered together with the income-tax filing reference and the professional e-procedures access (espace abonné).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SARL is subject by default to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) at 25% for fiscal year 2025, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for an eligible SME (turnover up to EUR 10 million and at least 75% of capital held by individuals). France applies the territoriality principle of Article 209-I CGI: only profits arising from operations carried out in France are taxable, while profits of a foreign permanent establishment are generally exempt, which is relevant to an arbitrage trader with foreign vessels and lifting points.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or comparable entity-classification election exists under French law. Available elections: (i) option for pass-through individual income tax (Article 239 bis AA CGI) for a closely-held SARL (natural persons holding at least 50% of the share capital, maximum 50 shareholders, corporate shareholders limited to 34% of capital), valid for 5 fiscal years — generally not recommended for export arbitrage due to the loss of the 15% reduced IS rate; (ii) election to apply the VAT franchise exemption (Article 293 B CGI) — available until the annual turnover threshold is exceeded but incompatible with export activity because it bars input-VAT recovery; (iii) option for the simplified (régime simplifié) or normal (régime réel normal) corporate tax filing regime; (iv) mandatory self-assessment of import VAT (reverse charge under Article 1695 CGI), in force since 1 January 2022 — eliminates the cash-flow burden on the import of raw cane sugar; (v) tax integration (intégration fiscale) under Articles 223 A et seq. CGI for a French parent holding at least 95% of its French subsidiaries — an optional group regime; (vi) hybrid mismatch protection: France transposed ATAD (Articles 209-IX, 212 bis and 212 quater CGI) — no election exists, but an entity may file protective documentation and, in a dual-inclusion income case, apply the minority-interest or trading-limitation rule of Article 212 bis-III CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), applied under the French General Tax Code (CGI, Articles 256 to 293) and the EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 91,900 (2025) annual turnover for supplies of goods, and EUR 37,500 for services (franchise en base de TVA under Article 293 B CGI); reduced thresholds: EUR 101,000 and EUR 41,000. Mandatory registration regardless of turnover applies to exporters of goods, intra-EU traders, and any company that must deduct input VAT; a physical-vessel sugar wholesale trader is therefore obliged to register for VAT from the first shipment and cannot rely on the franchise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured e-invoicing (facturation électronique) for all domestic B2B supplies from 1 September 2026 (all undertakings must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-size enterprises must issue them) and from 1 September 2027 for every enterprise, including SMEs. Invoices must be transmitted via a certified Dematerialisation Platform Partner (PDP) or the government's Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), using a structured format compliant with EN 16931 (Factur-X / UBL). Cross-border transaction and payment data (e-reporting) is filed electronically with the DGFiP through the PPF. France does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system (unlike Italy or Latin America); compliance is ensured by periodic CA3 VAT returns and DES/ESA recapitulative statements filed via EDI or impots.gouv.fr. The PPF API specifications (PPF-API v1.0) apply to platform-to-platform transmissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Articles 262-I-1° and 262 ter-I CGI, supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU (physical export) and intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered customer are exempt with the right to deduct input tax (effective 0%). Conditions for the SARL: (i) the sugar must be delivered to a purchaser established outside France or the EU; (ii) the goods must physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter must hold proof of export within the deadlines set by BOI-TVA-EXPORT-20-10-20; (iii) export invoices carry the Incoterms and vessel details; and (iv) for sugar imported into France for re-export, the import must be declared under a suspensive customs procedure (customs warehousing, transit) or the mandatory import-VAT reverse charge under Article 1695 CGI must be self-assessed to neutralise the cash flow. Offshore chain transactions where the raw sugar never enters French customs territory are outside the scope of French VAT (Article 258-2 CGI). For EU refiners as customers, the intra-EU zero-rating requires the customer's valid VAT ID on the invoice, the goods dispatched to another EU state, and the EU recapitulative statement (ESA/DES) to be filed. Where a tariff-rate quota or preferential origin is claimed for raw cane sugar, the commodity must comply with the relevant EU import-licence or TRQ allocation certificate and the qualitative polarization specification of the Common Market Organisation (Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation, DAE/DEX) accepted and discharged by the DGDDI in the DELTA-X / Export single window, with clean exit status and date of release
Bill of Lading (connaissement maritime) — original or recognised electronic (e-B/L) evidencing EU port of loading, non-EU port of discharge, vessel name, consignee and freight terms
Commercial invoice and packing list stating the buyer, Incoterm, quantity, polarization and quality of the VHP raw cane sugar
Export contract and purchase order (or the Revolving LC / Swift Wire instruction) evidencing the foreign counterparty and the terms of sale
Inward remittance or settlement evidence — SWIFT MT103, conformity certificate or LC utilisation statement showing receipt of the foreign-currency proceeds

Sugar-specific trade documentation where relevant: EU import/export licence, TRQ allocation certificate, non-preferential or preferential certificate of origin and the refining-end-use declaration for raw cane sugar
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may within the standard three-year assessment period (Articles L. 169 and L. 176 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales — LPF, extended to 6 years for non-filed declarations and to 10 years where the export activity is carried on abroad or through an offshore vehicle) re-examine the export file and, if the documentary bundle is incomplete, falsified or untimely, reverse the 0% rate. Consequences: (i) reassessment to the standard 20% VAT, plus monthly late interest of 0.2% (Article 1727 CGI); (ii) penalties of 40% for bad faith (mauvaise foi) or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses) under Article 1729 CGI; (iii) application of the abuse-of-law procedure (Articles L. 64 and L. 64 A LPF) for artificial schemes, adding an 80% penalty and a fine of EUR 10,000 to EUR 100,000; (iv) criminal prosecution under Articles 1741-1742 CGI for fraudulent VAT evasion, punishable by five years' imprisonment and a cumulative fine of EUR 500,000 (aggravated to seven years and EUR 2 million in cases of organised fraud); (v) customs sanctions under the Code des Douanes for materially inaccurate export declarations — confiscation of goods, a fine of up to twice the value of the goods, and withdrawal of the exporter's customs authorisation; (vi) for sugar, the loss of the licence security or guarantee and exclusion from future TRQ allocations. Company directors and de facto managers may be held jointly liable for the tax debt (Article L. 267 LPF) in the event of serious or repeated mismanagement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the national monetary authority operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) retains sovereign competence for financial relations with foreign states under the Code monétaire et financier; the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) licenses and supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic-money institutions in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts in France. No exchange-control authorization is required for trade settlement, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or loan servicing, pursuant to Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Residual constraints are exclusively declarative: (i) EU cash-transport declarations above EUR 10,000 under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672, (ii) Banque de France balance-of-payments cotation reporting by the paying bank, (iii) EU/OFAC sanctions screening, and (iv) disclosure of foreign-located accounts on French Form 3916. A French SARL may remit dividends to non-resident shareholders without prior approval, subject to the domestic 25% withholding tax which may be reduced or eliminated under tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France has abolished any mandatory surrender of export proceeds; the SARL may retain 100% of receipts in EUR or in foreign currency within authorized comptes en devises, with no statutory conversion timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no authorized-dealer retention limit. The only binding obligations are statistical and fiscal: the paying bank must codify every export collection under the Banque de France balance-of-payments cotation catalogue using the merchandise-export classification, and the company must declare any fully foreign-located account on Form 3916 attached to its annual corporate tax return.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for operational collections, FX conversion, and administrative disbursements; LOW for vessel-scale LC and trade-finance mandates. ACPR-licensed and PSD2-passported EMIs (Qonto, Shine, Wise Business, Ebury, Airwallex) permit fully remote multi-currency onboarding, SEPA Instant, sponsored SWIFT wires, and competitive USD/EUR conversion, but they cannot issue or confirm UCP600 documentary credits, lack direct SWIFT membership, commonly impose per-transfer ceilings incompatible with 12,000-15,000 mt sugar parcel settlements, and offer no commodity trade-finance intermediation. The compliant structure is a tandem model: EMI for sub-EUR 50,000 payment legs and receivables, with the French Tier-1 bank hosting the escrow account, revolving LC, USD clearing account, and FX hedging line.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: ACPR doctrine (L'identification à distance, effective from 2019 and reinforced by AMLD6 transposition in Article R312-2 of the Code monétaire et financier) legally permits full remote video-identification for corporate accounts. In practice, Tier-1 French banks contractually impose, under internal AML risk-adaptation, at least one physical interview of one gérant and the natural-person UBO when shareholders are foreign legal entities, funding derives from cross-border commodity arbitrage, or projected settlement volume exceeds EUR 1 million per annum. Remote onboarding of a second manager using notarized and apostilled powers of attorney is generally accepted. The preparatory dossier must include the apostilled certificate of incorporation, RBE registration receipt, audited parent accounts, and banking reference letters; directors should budget for one physical visit to Paris or Le Havre or to the bank's dedicated trade-finance branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign corporate UBO chain lacking verifiable French operational substance (red flag under Article L561-5 of the Code monétaire et financier).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled parent incorporation certificate; notarized share-register extract identifying the natural-person UBO; French RBE filing receipt evidencing the greater-than-25% ownership chain; three years of audited parent financial statements; bank reference letters from two regulated institutions in the ownership jurisdiction; and a signed economic-rationale letter mapping suppliers, off-takers, incoterms, and freight routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value trade payments executing before the complete trade-file documentation is delivered (conduit-transaction or supplier-substitute suspicion).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-completed trade file comprising the signed purchase contract (FOB Santos or CFR basis with polarization price formula), proforma invoice, revolving-LC term sheet, GFSC/GSP certificate of origin, VHP raw-sugar specification sheet (polarization above 99.4 degrees, moisture below 0.15%, ash below 0.15%), load-port appointment telegram, and the prior fixture file demonstrating continuity of genuine physical trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional risk of the UBO or of sugar-origin counterparties (FATF high-risk or grey-list rating, or beneficiary-bank concentration risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved counterparty whitelist with full entity KYC; OFAC and EU Consolidated List screening certificates; vessel IMO, flag, and AIS transponder due-diligence report; routing confirmation through the French bank's correspondent branch in the origin jurisdiction; and an end-user or final-destination attestation covering the discharged cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity of the equity injection into a no-minimum-capital SARL at formation or at a subsequent capital increase.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attestation de dépôt de fonds issued by the depositary bank or notary at incorporation; notarized statuts; board resolutions of the corporate shareholder authorizing the contribution; treasury and bank statements evidencing provenance through a regulated financial institution; and a declaration of absence of encumbrances on the share register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Circular-trade or repeated same-counterparty concentration pattern in bulk-commodity USD LC requests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Series of take-or-pay purchase agreements; independent inspection certificates from SGS, Intertek, or Cotecna covering weight, quality, and load-hold cleanliness; one fully settled historical LC documentary set demonstrating physical delivery; GAFTA or RSA arbitration-clause extracts; and supply-chain mapping anchored to the master bill-of-lading trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions and shareholder subordinated-loan injections may enter France by SEPA transfer for EUR or by SWIFT MT103 for USD and third currencies without prior authorization. The receiving bank applies the Banque de France cotation classification: equity subscription is coded as a direct-investment operation, intercompany loans under the financial-credit class, and commercial prepayments against sugar cargo under merchandise-trade codes. Field 70 of the MT103 must carry the SARL's SIREN/SIRET, the contract or LC reference, and the UBO's RBE identifier. Any cash component equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 triggers the mandatory declaration duty under Article L561-15 of the Code monétaire et financier. Formation capital must be held in a blocked account opened in the SARL's name, with the attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the depositary institution before RCS registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) irrevocable revolving documentary letters of credit governed by UCP600, issued by the French Tier-1 bank in favor of the origin seller for each 12,000-15,000 mt VHP raw-cane-sugar parcel, typically 90-180 days usance; (ii) SWIFT MT103 wires for premium, demurrage, and open-account margin balances, annotated with the merchandise-import purpose text and contract references; (iii) standby letters of credit under ISP98 for performance and price-adjustment undertakings; and (iv) cash-against-documents settlement through the load-port agent for spot purchases. The SARL may additionally access forfaiting of the LC-accepted USD bills of exchange to release liquidity without disrupting the delivery schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright FX forward (30-180 day tenors) settling the USD payable on each revolving-LC maturity, booked under ISDA/CSA documentation with the French Tier-1 bank and subject to EMIR margin rules.
EUR/USD FX swap (spot-versus-forward, tom-next, or rolling forward) for intra-maturity liquidity mismatches between USD LC disbursements and EUR operating cash.
EUR/USD OTC vanilla currency options (purchased puts on USD payables) with premium payment, classified as hedging-only under MiFID II professional-client eligibility.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD referencing BRL (Brazilian real), THB (Thai baht), or COP (Colombian peso) where origin-side cost exposure in less-convertible markets requires offshore hedging, with settlement in EUR.
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (EUR/USD CCIRS) to refinance the LC usance and forfaiting facility into matched-currency funding for extended tenors.

Price-plus-FX combined commodity swap on ICE Futures No. 11 world raw-sugar differentials with an embedded EUR/USD conversion clause, executed on a regulated EU trading venue or as an EMIR-cleared swap.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Infogreffe (transmitted to INSEE RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the anniversary of the SARL's RCS registration, on an annual basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission triggers a formal regularization notice; continued non-confirmation may lead to a court-ordered radiation (strike-off) from the RCS and loss of legal existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registre du commerce et des sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months of financial year-end (mandatory before the annual shareholder meeting); calendar-year SARL: by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is punishable by a fine up to EUR 15,000; repeated omission can result in a court summon of the manager, and eventual strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Liasse fiscale n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar year-end: electronic filing by the second business day after 1 May (typically 3 May); non-calendar year: within three months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of corporate tax due (10% if unreported after a 30-day formal notice); failure to file may result in automatic assessment and interest for delay.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SARL when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4,000,000, turnover exclusive of VAT greater than EUR 8,000,000, and average workforce greater than 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies when the SARL controls or is controlled by an entity requiring consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts must comply with the Plan Comptable Général (PCG / French GAAP). Consolidated accounts, where applicable, are prepared in accordance with IFRS as adopted by the European Union.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO re-filing is required in France. A declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be updated with the RCS within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. The annual Confirmation annuelle d'activité reconfirms the registered data. Internally, share transfers must be recorded in the registre des associés and reflected in the public registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers and Directors (Registre des gérants/décisions)
